title: Tenali Raman and the Banquet in the Dark

full_text:
Following an unexpected spike in municipal lamp-oil taxes, poor artisans and weavers in Vijayanagara could no longer afford oil for evening lamps, forcing their families to eat dinner and work in total darkness.
When Tenali Raman raised the issue in council, King Krishnadevaraya dismissed it lightly:
'What difference does a little darkness make? One eats with one’s mouth, not with one’s eyes! A sensible man can find his rice in the dark without complaining!'

Tenali Raman smiled politely and said nothing.
Two days later, Tenali invited King Krishnadevaraya and five senior ministers to an 'Exclusive Imperial Royal Banquet' at his house at nightfall.

The King and ministers arrived dressed in fine silks.
They were seated around a low table upon velvet floor cushions.
Before the food was brought in, Tenali quietly extinguished every single oil lamp and candle in the house, shuttered all windows, and bolted the doors, plunging the room into pitch-black, absolute darkness!

The King blinked in confusion: 'Tenali! Why hast thou extinguished the lamps? It is pitch black!'

Tenali’s voice echoed from the shadows:
'Maharaj! Remember your royal wisdom spoken in council: "One eats with one’s mouth, not with one’s eyes!"
To honor your philosophy, tonight’s royal feast is served in total darkness!'

Servants placed large banana leaves before each guest in the dark, laden with hot, spicy curries, sticky rice, rasam, and sweet, runny payasam.
The hungry King and ministers attempted to eat:
In the pitch-black room, chaos immediately ensued!
The King tried to scoop up rice, but plunged his fingers directly into a bowl of burning hot, spicy rasam: 'Ouch! My fingers!'
Minister Chandrashekar reached for a sweet laddu, but grabbed the Prime Minister’s knee instead!
Another minister brought his hand up to eat, missed his mouth completely, and shoved a handful of sticky, sweet payasam straight into his own left eye and mustache!
Curry spilled onto silk dhotis, water jugs were overturned, and courtiers bumped heads in the dark, groaning and grumbling!

King Krishnadevaraya shouted in exasperation:
'Tenali! Light the lamps this instant! We cannot eat a single bite without smearing curry across our faces!'

Tenali struck a flint and lit a row of bright brass lamps.
The sight revealed was hilarious:
The King’s mustache was dripping with sweet pudding, the ministers were splattered with yellow dal and red chili curry, looking like bruised circus clowns!

The King looked around at his stained ministers, then looked at Tenali standing with folded hands.
The Emperor felt a deep, humble realization.
Tenali spoke softly:
'Maharaj, if the greatest Emperor in India and his noble ministers cannot eat dinner in the dark for ten minutes without burning their fingers and spilling their food, imagine the misery of thousands of poor weavers, potters, and children forced to spend their nights in darkness because of an unjust tax on lamp oil.'

King Krishnadevaraya wiped the pudding from his face, embraced Tenali, and immediately abolished the lamp-oil tax, ordering free oil distributed to poor artisans.
The people blessed Tenali Raman for bringing light to their homes through the magic of a darkened feast.
moral: A ruler must understand the daily hardships of his subjects; tasting darkness teaches empathy.
